newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut hotel executive returns after disappearance.
newsitem.headline: Beirut hotel executive returns after disappearance.

text.p: A Beirut hotel executive who disappeared three weeks ago after being seized by unknown men returned home on Saturday but refused to say who had held him.
An official of the Beirut Marriott Hotel told Reuters on Sunday that its financial controller Derar al-Karmi returned home at 9.30 p.m. on Saturday but did not want to talk about his experience.
"He's not saying anything...the Marriott doesnt want to say anything either," the official said. "He doesn't want to meet the press."
Karmi was taken from the Marriott on January 3 by three men in plain clothes. As he was leaving he whispered to a colleague that the men were "Mukhabarat" (secret police).
Hotel officials said during his disappearance they were unable to find out who was holding Karmi, a Palestinian-born Jordanian aged abut 40 who has worked for 15 years for the Marriott group.
Jordan protested to the Lebanese government over his disappearance.
Beirut newspapers speculated that Karmi was being questioned about an attack on Syrian workers in Lebanon before Christmas and a bus bombing in Damascus that killed 11 people.
Lebanon's prosecutor-general Adnan Addoum told reporters last week Karmi had been detained on orders of the military judicial authorities, but said he did not know who was holding him or where.
